chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā ibn ʿUbayd, who said:
I and Ibn Faḍḍāl were sitting when Yūnus approached and said: “I entered upon Abū al-Ḥasan al-Riḍā عليه السلام and said to him, ‘May I be your ransom, the people have spoken much about the pillar.’”

He said: “So he said to me, ‘O Yūnus, what do you think it is? Do you regard it as a pillar of iron raised for your companion?’” He said: “I said, ‘I do not know.’” He said: “‘Rather, it is an angel entrusted with every city; Allah raises the deeds of that city by means of him.’”
He said: “Then Ibn Faḍḍāl stood, kissed his head, and said, ‘May Allah have mercy on you, O Abū Muḥammad. You never cease bringing the true hadith through which Allah relieves us.’”

key_terms.الْحَدِيثِ الْحَقِّ: the true hadith that clarifies reality
key_terms.عَمُودًا: a pillar, here negated as a literal iron structure
key_terms.مَلَكٌ: an angel appointed for a specific function

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith of Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام say about the ‘pillar’ and the raising of people’s deeds?
ai.summary: This hadith records Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام clarifying that what people referred to as the ‘pillar’ was not a physical iron column, but an angel appointed over each city through whom Allah raises the deeds of its people. The report highlights unseen divine administration and the role of the Imams عليهم السلام in correcting mistaken conceptions with true hadith.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa Bin Ubeyd who said,

‘It was so that I and Ibn Fazzal were seated when Yunus came over and he said, ‘I went over to Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> and I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! The people are frequently (speaking) regarding the pillar (of light)’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘O Yunus! What do you see it as? Do you see it as a pillar of iron raised for your companions?’ I said, ‘I do not know’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But, it is an Angel allocated with every city. Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Raises the deeds of that city with him’.

He (the narrator) said, ‘So Ibn Fazzal stood up and kissed his head and said, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> have Mercy on you, O Abu Muhammad<sup>asws</sup>! You<sup>asws</sup> do not cease to come with the true Hadeeth by which Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Relieves from us’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa ibn ‘Ubayd who has said the following.

“I and ibn Faddal were sitting tha Yunus came and said, ‘I went to see abu al-Hassan al-Rida (a.s.) and said to him, “May Allah take my soul in service for your cause, “People speak so much about pillar.”

He said to me, “O Yunus, what do you see? Do you see it as a pillar of iron that you would raise for your friend?” The narrator has said that he said, “I do not know.” The Imam (a.s.) said, “In fact, it is an appointed angel in every town. Through him Allah raises the deeds of that town.”

The narrator has said that ibn Faddal then stood up and kissed his head and said, “May allah grant you blessings, O abu Muhammad, you continue to bring us true hadith with which Allah grants us relief and comfort.”
